_what: FLOWS — a new record type. Nicolas, 5 Sep: 'I would also create this video as a flow.'
_definition: A flow is an ORDERED SEQUENCE worked through in one session, aimed at one skill. It is not a ladder (that is one movement getting harder), not a complex (that is a loaded circuit for conditioning), and not a protocol (that is a prescription like Zone 2). A flow is how you spend a session when the goal is to learn something.
_honesty: The flare flow below is built from the DOCUMENTED prerequisites for the move — straddle flexibility, straddle strength, planche-position arm support, hip circles — not from watching the video, which I cannot do. Check it against the tutorial and tell me what is missing or out of order.

flows.name: The Flare
flows.source: Leo Moves — Break Dance Flare, step-by-step tutorial
flows.why: The flare is a compression skill wearing a dance costume. Almost all of the work is straddle strength and the shoulder shift — the spin is the last five percent.
steps: Non-negotiable. Every rung below puts bodyweight through an extended wrist.
Open the straddle first. You cannot train a range you do not have.
Turn that range into strength. This is the single most transferable drill here.
Hold what you just lifted. Hands down, legs up and wide.
The flare lives in a planche-lean shoulder position. Build the support before the spin.
Slow. The whole skill is the weight transfer from hand to hand.
Front half only, set down, reset. Quality over continuity.
Five honest attempts, then stop. This is a skill session, not a conditioning session.
